answer.explanation: A session (pid 87) executed `BEGIN; LOCK TABLE orders IN ACCESS EXCLUSIVE MODE; SELECT pg_sleep(3600);` and has been holding that transaction open for ~40s (and will for up to an hour). This ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock blocks every other statement that touches the `orders` table, including the simple `SELECT id, item, status FROM orders ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 10` used by GET /orders. Those queries (pids 88, 114, 122, 150) are all queued behind the lock (wait_event Lock/relation), so the API's GET /orders requests never get a response from postgres and hang until the client's 15s timeout fires. POST /jobs and other endpoints are unaffected because they don't touch the locked `orders` table, matching the alert pattern exactly.
